chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who directed that Hajj al-Islam be performed on his behalf, but the total of what he left did not exceed fifty dirhams. He said: 'Hajj is performed on his behalf from some of the stations that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated, from near [Makkah].'

key_terms.مِنْ قُرْبٍ: From near (referring to Miqat al-Qurb, closer to Makkah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a deceased person's estate is too small to cover the full cost of Hajj?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify the flexibility in fulfilling the deceased's Hajj obligation when resources are scarce, emphasizing that the validity of the pilgrimage is not contingent upon the full financial capacity but rather on performing the essential rites from the nearest Miqat. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in acts of worship, ensuring that the spiritual debt is discharged proportionally to the available estate without imposing undue hardship on the heirs or the performer.
